name: How much contingency should I budget for a commercial remodel in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: How much contingency should I budget for a commercial remodel in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: How much contingency should I budget for a commercial remodel in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: For Los Angeles commercial remodels, contingency is one of the most important budget items because older buildings often reveal hidden conditions once demolition starts. Common surprises include outdated wiring, damaged framing, unrecorded plumbing, asbestos or other environmental issues, and code-required upgrades tied to the new scope. The right contingency depends on whether the project is a light refresh, a full tenant improvement, or a deeper renovation involving structural or systems work. Owners should also account for escalation in labor and materials, design revisions, and potential change orders if field conditions differ from the drawings. A contractor should explain which risks are included in the base price and which are excluded. The most useful budgeting approach is to combine a defined scope with a realistic reserve instead of using the lowest bid alone. Projects in occupied buildings or high-traffic neighborhoods can also carry higher indirect costs from phasing, staging, and limited work hours.
acceptedAnswer.description: A commercial remodel budget should usually include a contingency because existing buildings often hide conditions that are not visible at bid time. Many owners set aside an extra percentage for demolition surprises, code upgrades, material changes, and permit revisions, with the amount depending on project age and scope.
